items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: I have played second to Rene. I played second to Buddy too at times, you know.

ctx.x: Well, what about guys like Chris and Buddy and... Who was that guy? Chris and Buddy and Rene and all those, would you play any second trumpet to them ever?

I have played second to Rene. I played second to Buddy too at times, you know. Most of the time, sometimes they'd split, they'd get in, they'd had so much work to it was. At that time, they'd split the band, you see. They'd send me either with the bass and they'd hire out the different ones, you know. You know, on them spot jobs, and they needed trumpet player, well they'd hire me. In fact, Rene taken the liking to me, I started playing following his, and I guess that's about what it was, you see, and I couldn't…
Remember any of the guys that Rene would have in his band?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: And I worked with Rene, I worked with Buddy.

ctx.x: But Rene didn't teach you out of a book or anything? No, no, no. Just show you out of a book.

By hearing finger into the trumpet. Starling, you know? And I worked with Rene, I worked with Buddy. You know, these bands at that time, when they were short of a man, well they'd hire, and if I was passable enough to hold a job they'd put them in their place or so. You understand? They'd get two jobs, they'd split up some of them men and send on a job with a would-be player, you understand? A beginner or something like that and break him in. That's the way that piece would work. In other words, they'd collect…

items.title: De De Pierce Interview, 1960-01-10
items.q: Is that Buddy's stepfather or uncle or something?

ctx.x: I forget his name, old man Petit. He played a bit.
Is that Buddy's stepfather or uncle or something? Stepfather or uncle or something.
Something else in relation. That's Joe Petit. That's Joe Petit. That's Joe Petit, yeah.
